Vs

full_judgment: 28. In the instant case there is no direct evidence. Prosecution witness Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 14 are formal and official witnesses and prosecution witness No. 10 Ilias, the husband of the Razia Khatoon, was tendered but not cross-examined by the prosecution and prosecution witness No. 11 had been tendered, prosecution witness Nos. 7 and 15 are formal witnesses and prosecution witnesses Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 had been declared hostile. In a case where the direct evidence is not available it has to be dealt with on the basis of the circumstantial evidence to connect a particular person with the alleged occurrence. Further, in a case of murder where the prosecution is required to prove the case solely depending on the circumstantial evidence the law required with precision the co-existence of the 'chain' of circumstances, 'compatibility' of the same, fortified with the 'motive' to establish the foundation of the prosecution case. These are the ingredients treading on the path of long established principle of criminal jurisprudence finally accepted as the settled principle of law. The slightest deviation from the totalness of these elements invariably renders prosecution case highly improbable and unsustainable. Keeping behind the above principle if we assess the present case we see, as we have already observed, that there is no direct evidence to connect the accused appellant Nekbar with the murder of the deceased Razia Khatoon in the manner described by the informant PW 1 in the first information report. Prosecution, in order to prove the alleged murder beyond reasonable doubt, had to rely on the circumstantial evidence and all other attending reality of the case. Now if we analyse the evidence of different PWs we find that from the deposition of PW 1 informant and PW 7, two formal witnesses, there is no iota of evidence to the effect that the deceased Razia Khatoon was enticed by the accused appellant in the manner depicted in the first information report. PW 7 in his cross-examination in reply to the question from the defence categorically mentioned that there are two rival groups in the village one of which is guided by the appellant side and the other one by the informant side. He also stated in his cross that he could not remember the date of 'Salish', all he could say that he was present in the 'Salish'. All other witnesses who were declared hostile when examined by the prosecution stated that they only heard about the enticement of the deceased Razia Khatoon by the accused appellant Nekbar and nothing more than that. Nowhere from the evidence it could be gathered that Razia Khatoon was enticed by the appellant and subsequently offered to her husband to take her back. On the other hand most important witness PW 10, Ilias, husband of the deceased Razia Khatoon was surprisingly tendered by the prosecution and was not cross-examined. This act from the side of the prosecution is really unfortunate which gives a strong presumption of improbability of the prosecution case within the meaning of section 114G of the Evidence Act. PW 10, who was the husband of the deceased, was the proper witness who could reveal the truth or falsity of the case, particularly the fact of enticing the deceased Razia Khatoon by the accused appellant Nekbar. The learned Additional Sessions Judge though, observed this vital lacuna of the prosecution regarding the non-examination of PW 10, did not give benefit of the same in favour of the accused appellant. He should have been given benefit of doubt on that score.
